Topic at a glance
Domestic Disciplinary Enquiry, Misconduct and Natural Justice is a registered theme in Labour & Industrial Law. Domestic Disciplinary Enquiry, Misconduct and Natural Justice is governed by Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, Code on Wages, 2019 and Trade Unions Act, 1926, subject to commencement and applicable transition rules of labour codes. identify the statute actually in force for the dispute, the date of termination or wage liability, the appropriate Government and the conciliation or reference stage.

Courtroom and evidentiary roadmap
Competent forum: the appropriate Government, Labour Court, Industrial Tribunal, National Tribunal, civil court where jurisdiction survives, or constitutional court according to the dispute and statutory route. the party asserting workman status, industry, termination, retrenchment, unfair labour practice or wage entitlement must establish the foundational employment facts; statutory presumptions and records may shift evidentiary burdens. Where electronic records are relied upon, apply BSA 2023 s. 63 and the applicable burden provisions without treating electronic admissibility as proof of the ultimate fact.
